record.original_question: For a separable II_1 factor N and a positive scalar t, do N and its amplification N^t have the same number of sequential commutation orbits of Haar unitaries?

evidence.quote: Problem 29. Let N be a separable II1 factor. Then do N and Nt have the same number of sequential commutation orbits?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $N$ be a separable $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor with unique normal faithful tracial state $\tau$. A unitary $u \in N$ is called a Haar unitary if $\tau(u^n) = 0$ for every nonzero integer $n$. Fix a free ultrafilter $\omega$ on $\mathbb{N}$ and let $N^\omega$ denote the tracial ultrapower of $N$. Define an equivalence relation on the set of Haar unitaries of $N$ as follows: two Haar unitaries $u, v \in N$ are equivalent if there exist Haar unitaries $w_0, w_1, \ldots, w_k \in N^\omega$ with $w_0 = u$, $w_k = v$, and $[w_{i-1}, w_i] = 0$ for $i = 1, \ldots, k$ (a "sequential commutation path"). Call the equivalence classes the sequential commutation orbits of $N$.

For $t > 0$, let $N^t$ denote the amplification of $N$ (i.e., $p(N \otimes B(\ell^2))p$ for a projection $p$ of trace $t$ when $t \le 1$, with the standard extension for $t > 1$).

Question: For every separable $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor $N$ and every $t > 0$, do $N$ and $N^t$ have the same number of sequential commutation orbits of Haar unitaries?
artifact.status_search_result: The notion of sequential commutation orbits for Haar unitaries in tracial von Neumann algebras was introduced recently, with the basic dichotomy (1 orbit vs. uncountably many) and structural results established for free group factors and Gamma factors. The question of invariance of the number of orbits under amplification appears as one of the listed open problems and no resolution was found in the search results.

status_evidence.title: Sequential commutation in tracial von Neumann algebras
status_evidence.snippet: introduces an equivalence relation on Haar unitaries in a diffuse tracial von Neumann algebra via finite paths of sequentially commuting Haar unitaries in an ultrapower; shows the relation has 1 or uncountably many orbits.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the framework of sequential commutation orbits but does not resolve invariance under amplification.

status_evidence.title: Internal sequential commutation and single generation
status_evidence.snippet: Further develops sequential commutation and the commutation diameter invariant.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work continues studying the invariant; amplification invariance not established here.
